The test *failed* as expected, with an `AssertionError` showing the difference in the key `[keys .'a'.'c']` versus `[keys.'a'.'c']`. This confirms that the whitespace around the dot notation is indeed lost.

This test correctly identifies the bug and will pass once the bug is fixed. I can now confidently provide the final test file.", "final_test": "import pytest\nfrom tomlkit import dumps, parse\n\n\ndef test_whitespace_preservation_in_keys():\n    content = \"\"\"\n[keys.a]\n#    ↓ this whitespace disappears\n[keys .'a'.'c']\n  'd'\t= 'e'\n\"\"\"\n    doc = parse(content)\n\n    # The bug description implies that reassigning breaks the structure\n    # and causes whitespace to be lost.\n    # The original issue's example uses a loop, so we'll replicate that.\n    for mode in doc[\"keys\"]:\n        doc[\"keys\"][mode] = doc[\"keys\"][mode]\n\n    # The bug is that the whitespace around 'a'.'c' is lost.\n    # If the bug is present, dumps(doc) will NOT be equal to content.\n    # Therefore, to make the test FAIL at the buggy commit, we assert equality.\n    # When the bug is fixed, dumps(doc) WILL be equal to content, and the test will pass.\n    assert dumps(doc) == content\n"}
